answer: Each identity must seal a unique piece of data and periodically prove it still holds a distinct copy, so one operator with a thousand identities must store a thousand genuinely different sealed sectors rather than pointing the same cheap disk at a thousand names. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns a jetty, answers a nebula, and is named by a prism: a farm can mint prism bindings instantly, but the jetty behind each one is disk, and the nebula will catch the ones that share it. The attacker therefore pays for real storage per head.
